- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility events.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then gradually decline, missing sudden drops or sharp reversals.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overcorrects after large deviations, leading to premature flattening of price trajectories.
- Overshoots occur after high volatility days; model fails to account for lagged market reactions to policy or supply shocks.
- Forecasts often underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections following spikes, especially in the 3rd–5th day post-event.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the first 5–7 days after a spike, leading to overly optimistic mid-term forecasts.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the 10–15 day horizon, suggesting failure to capture long-term supply/demand equilibrium adjustments.
- Model fails to adjust for sudden policy or regulatory changes — forecasts remain static despite real-time market shocks.
- Forecasts exhibit “sticky” behavior — resist downward corrections even when true prices show clear downward momentum.
- Model overfits short-term trends, leading to overconfidence in mid-term forecasts, especially when true prices show mean-reverting behavior.
